```{r fig3-build}
# unchanged rather than special-cased, because cross-section consistency is worth
# more than one prettier label.
COPRO_GENERA <- c("Sordaria","Podospora","Cercophora","Chaetomium","Schizothecium",
                  "Preussia","Delitschia","Pilobolus","Ascobolus","Saccobolus",
                  "Sporormiella","Coprinopsis","Thelebolus","Coniochaeta")
gen       <- strip_rank(tax$Genus[match(top5$OTU, rownames(tax))])
gen       <- ifelse(gen %in% c("", "NA"), NA, gen)
guild_str <- funguild_otu$Guild[match(top5$OTU, funguild_otu$OTU_ID)]
is_copro  <- (!is.na(guild_str) & grepl("Dung Saprotroph", guild_str)) |
             (!is.na(gen)       & gen %in% COPRO_GENERA)
is_plant  <- !is_copro & !is.na(guild_str) &
             grepl("Endophyte|Plant Saprotroph|Plant Pathogen|Epiphyte", guild_str)
is_patho  <- !is_copro & !is_plant & !is.na(guild_str) & grepl("Pathogen|Parasite", guild_str)
top5$Guild <- factor(
  ifelse(is_copro, "Dung saprotroph",
  ifelse(is_plant, "Plant-associated",
  ifelse(is_patho, "Pathotroph",
  ifelse(!is.na(guild_str), "Other assigned", "Unassigned / dark")))),
  levels = GUILD_LEVELS)

# The two seasons' top-5 sets are disjoint, so one global factor ordered
# (Season, share) gives each facet its own descending bars under free_y.
top5 <- top5[order(top5$Season, top5$share), ]
top5$label <- factor(top5$label, levels = top5$label)
n_lab <- setNames(sprintf("%s (n = %d)", levels(season_c), as.integer(table(season_c))),
                  levels(season_c))

pD <- ggplot(top5, aes(share, label, fill = Guild)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%  (%d/%d)", share, n_detect, n_season)),
            hjust = -0.12, size = 2.8, colour = "grey25") +
  facet_grid(Season ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
             labeller = labeller(Season = n_lab)) +
  # drop = TRUE: "Other assigned" has no member among these ten OTUs and a key
  # with no bar is noise; the level ORDER stays the repo-canonical one.
  scale_fill_manual(values = guild_cols, name = "Functional guild", drop = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.32))) +
  labs(x = "Mean within-season read share (%)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Bar labels give the mean share and, in parentheses,\nthe number of that season's samples with any detection.") +
  base_theme +
  theme(axis.text.y = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 9)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 2, nrow = 2))

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
# An explicit design grid, not nested `/` and `|`: patchwork FLATTENS a chain of
# `/`, so (pA / pB) / (pC | pD) silently becomes a three-row layout and errors.
# The grid also guarantees what panel A and B depend on -- one shared column
# geometry, so their facet columns line up and the slope flip reads vertically.
# D gets five of the eight columns because its taxon labels are up to 38 chars.
design <- "
AAAAAAAA
BBBBBBBB
CCCDDDDD
"
fig3 <- pA + pB + pC + pD +
  plot_layout(design = design, heights = c(1, 1.18, 1.55), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal")

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  one(function() grDevices::png(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                                units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  pdf_dev <- if (capabilities("cairo")) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  one(function() pdf_dev(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig3_richness_evenness_crossover"), fig3, 10, 10.4)

# ---- console summary -------------------------------------------------------
cat("Season-pool asymptotic diversity (Table S8):\n")
print(data.frame(q = Q_LEVELS,
                 summer = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", A_sum$TD_asy, A_sum$qTD.LCL, A_sum$qTD.UCL),
                 winter = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", A_win$TD_asy, A_win$qTD.LCL, A_win$qTD.UCL)),
      row.names = FALSE)
hill_means <- aggregate(cbind(q0, q1, q2) ~ Season, hill, mean)
hill_means[-1] <- round(hill_means[-1], 2)
cat(sprintf("\nPer-sample Hill means (n = %d, rarefied to %d reads):\n", nrow(hill), rfy_depth))
print(hill_means, row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nReplicate-level LMM, summer - winter (n = %d; Table S9):\n", n_pcr))
print(data.frame(metric = lmm$metric, delta = lmm$summer_minus_winter,
                 lwr = lmm$lwr, upr = lmm$upr, p = lmm$p), row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nTop-1 OTU read share: summer %.1f%% vs winter %.1f%%  (%s)\n",
            100 * obs_top1[["Summer"]], 100 * obs_top1[["Winter"]], pfmt(p_top1)))
cat(sprintf("Pielou evenness J   : summer %.2f  vs winter %.2f   (%s)\n",
            obs_J[["Summer"]], obs_J[["Winter"]], pfmt(p_J)))
cat("\nTop-5 OTUs per season (mean within-season read share):\n")
print(data.frame(Season = chk$Season, OTU = chk$OTU, share_pct = round(chk$share, 2),
                 detected = sprintf("%d/%d", chk$n_detect, chk$n_season),
                 guild = as.character(top5$Guild[match(chk$OTU, top5$OTU)])),
      row.names = FALSE)
```

### 10.4 Figure 4 — Dark and partly novel lineages dominate winter dung (E1)

*Provenance: all three panels come from Section 3.4. Fig. 4A and 4B are the main-text versions of Figures S-E1a and S-E1b; Fig. 4C plots Table S-E1b. Every value is read from the committed `tables/` CSVs written by `9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R` — nothing is recomputed from sequence data, because the Species Hypothesis assignment is an external pipeline step (a containerised run of the TU-NHM `sh_matching` workflow against the UNITE reference).*

![](figures/main/Fig4_dark_taxa_SH.png)

**Figure 4**: Winter dung is dominated by fungal lineages that carry no confident genus, a substantial fraction of which are genuinely novel. **(A)** Best-hit similarity of each OTU to its nearest UNITE Species Hypothesis, split into OTUs with no confident genus assignment ("dark"; n = 390 with a best hit) and those with one ("named"; n = 624). Each group's bars sum to 100% so the two shapes can be compared despite the different group sizes, and the y axis is square-root scaled so the divergent tail stays visible beneath the near-identical spike. The dark distribution is bimodal: 37% of dark OTUs sit at ≥ 99% identity to a reference — essentially known sequences whose genus was withheld by the conservative `minBoot = 80` threshold — while 38% fall below 95%, a genuinely divergent tail. The named distribution has the same spike (73% at ≥ 99%) but almost no tail (9% below 95%). OTUs with no best hit at all (103 dark, 12 named) cannot appear here; they are the "no SH match" and "ITSx-excluded" categories of (B). **(B)** UNITE Species Hypothesis placement of all 493 dark OTUs. **(C)** The 30 dark OTUs with the highest mean winter read share (Table S-E1b), plotted as prevalence — the number of the 26 winter samples with any detection — against that mean share, coloured as in (B). OTU1369 is labelled: it is winter's single most abundant OTU at 11.2% of winter reads and is present in 20 of 26 winter droppings, yet its best UNITE hit is only 85% similar, so it forms a candidate new Species Hypothesis rather than matching anything named.

Roughly half of a typical winter dropping is reads that the canonical taxonomy cannot name (Section 3.4), and panel A shows that this single label covers two different problems. A little over a third of dark OTUs are near-identical to a UNITE reference and are dark only because `minBoot = 80` declines to commit to a genus at that bootstrap — a cost of conservatism, and one that Species Hypothesis matching largely recovers. But a comparable fraction sits below 95% identity, where no threshold adjustment would help, and 228 of the 493 dark OTUs (46%) form candidate new Species Hypotheses rather than matching an existing one (panel B). The winter-abundant end of that distribution is what matters for this study: panel C shows that the dark OTUs carrying real winter read share are predominantly candidate-novel rather than placeable, and the most extreme of them, OTU1369, is simultaneously the most abundant and among the most prevalent OTUs in winter dung while being only 85% similar to its nearest named relative. Two caveats travel with the figure. "Candidate novel" is a statement about the reference database rather than a taxonomic claim: these are unimprinted clusters awaiting public sequence deposition and PlutoF registration (Section 3.4), so none of them yet carries a permanent identifier. And the 13 ITSx-excluded OTUs in (B) — among them OTU320, winter's third most abundant dark OTU — are flagged by the pipeline as chimeric or non-ITS; they are retained in (C) only because they remain in the abundance table, and should not be read as biological entities.

```{r fig4-build}
#| eval: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Full build code for Figure 4 — the source of truth for figures/main/Fig4_dark_taxa_SH.{png,jpg,pdf}"

# Figure 4 -- Winter dung is dominated by unclassified, partly novel lineages (E1).
# Every quantity here is READ from committed tables/ CSVs written by
# 9_dark_taxa_SH_matching.R; nothing is recomputed from sequence data, because the
# SH assignment itself is the expensive external step (a Singularity run of the
# TU-NHM sh_matching pipeline against the UNITE reference, ~90 min).
#   A  tables/dark_taxa_SH_matching.csv        (per-OTU similarity x is_dark)
#   B  tables/E1_SH_assignment_summary.csv     (the 493 dark OTUs' placement)
#   C  tables/E1_winter_dominant_dark_taxa_SH.csv (top 30 by winter read share)
# Guards below assert B and C are consistent with the per-OTU table in A.
# Rebuild:  conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig4-build

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(patchwork)
})

tab_dir <- if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
           "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables"
out_dir <- "figures/main"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
grDevices::pdf(NULL)                                 # headless: no X11 fallback

# ---- shared style ----------------------------------------------------------
# ONE colour dimension in this figure: SH placement, used by both B and C. Panel
# A compares two groups of OTUs, not two placements, so it is deliberately
# monochrome -- the darker fill is the dark taxa. That keeps every coloured mark
# in the figure meaning exactly one thing.
SH_LEVELS <- c("Placeable to existing SH", "Candidate novel SH",
               "No SH match", "ITSx-excluded")
sh_cols <- c("Placeable to existing SH" = "#0072B2",   # resolved
             "Candidate novel SH"       = "#D55E00",   # the novel signal
             "No SH match"              = "#999999",   # grey = no information,
             "ITSx-excluded"            = "#DDDDDD")   # as elsewhere in the repo
group_cols <- c("Named OTUs (genus assigned)"    = "#B8B8B8",
                "Dark OTUs (no confident genus)" = "#4D4D4D")

base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.spacing    = unit(0.8, "lines"),
        legend.key.size  = unit(0.42, "cm"),
        legend.title     = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.text      = element_text(size = 9))

# All in-plot text is ASCII: save_fig() falls back to grDevices::pdf when cairo is
# unavailable, and that device silently substitutes a dot for a Unicode glyph.
sh_class_map <- c(placeable_existing_SH = "Placeable to existing SH",
                  novel_new_SH          = "Candidate novel SH",
                  no_SH_match           = "No SH match",
                  excluded_nonITS       = "ITSx-excluded")

# ============================================================================
# Panel A -- best-hit similarity, dark vs named OTUs
# ============================================================================
sh <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "dark_taxa_SH_matching.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(is.logical(sh$is_dark), !anyNA(sh$is_dark), nrow(sh) == 1129L,
          all(sh$SH_class %in% names(sh_class_map)))

G_LEVELS <- c("Named OTUs (genus assigned)", "Dark OTUs (no confident genus)")
sh$group <- factor(ifelse(sh$is_dark, G_LEVELS[2], G_LEVELS[1]), levels = G_LEVELS)

# An OTU has a similarity only if the pipeline found a best hit at all: the
# no-match and ITSx-excluded OTUs of panel B have none by construction, so they
# cannot appear here. The caption says so, and these counts are printed below.
sim <- sh[!is.na(sh$similarity_percentage), ]
n_nosim <- table(sh$group[is.na(sh$similarity_percentage)])[G_LEVELS]
stopifnot(min(sim$similarity_percentage) >= 80, max(sim$similarity_percentage) <= 100)

# The histogram is precomputed rather than left to stat_bin, so the normalisation
# is explicit: each group's bars sum to 1, which is what lets a 390-OTU group be
# compared with a 624-OTU one. Bins are 1% wide over the pipeline's 80-100% range.
brks <- seq(80, 100, by = 1)
sim$bin <- cut(sim$similarity_percentage, breaks = brks, include.lowest = TRUE)
hist_df <- as.data.frame(table(group = sim$group, bin = sim$bin),
                         responseName = "n", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
hist_df$group <- factor(hist_df$group, levels = G_LEVELS)
hist_df$prop  <- ave(hist_df$n, hist_df$group, FUN = function(x) x / sum(x))
hist_df$mid   <- brks[-length(brks)][as.integer(factor(hist_df$bin, levels = levels(sim$bin)))] + 0.5
stopifnot(all(abs(tapply(hist_df$prop, hist_df$group, sum) - 1) < 1e-10))

# The two numbers that ARE the argument, per group: the near-identical spike and
# the divergent tail. Printed into the panel so the reader does not have to
# estimate them off the bars.
shape_lab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(G_LEVELS, function(g) {
  v <- sim$similarity_percentage[sim$group == g]
  data.frame(group = factor(g, levels = G_LEVELS),
             lab = sprintf("n = %d with a best hit\n%.0f%% at >= 99%% id   |   %.0f%% below 95%% id",
                           length(v), 100 * mean(v >= 99), 100 * mean(v < 95)),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

pA <- ggplot(hist_df, aes(mid, prop, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(data = shape_lab, aes(x = 80.2, y = Inf, label = lab), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, vjust = 1.25, size = 2.9, lineheight = 1.05, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(80, 100, 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))) +
  # Square-root y: the (99,100] bin alone holds 69% of named and 37% of dark
  # OTUs, and on a linear axis it flattens the divergent tail -- the half of the
  # argument that a linear axis would hide -- into the baseline.
  scale_y_sqrt(labels = scales::percent,
               breaks = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75),
               expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +
  labs(x = "Best-hit similarity to nearest UNITE species hypothesis (%)",
       y = "Share of the group's OTUs",
       subtitle = "Each group's bars sum to 100%, so the two shapes compare despite different group sizes.\nSquare-root y axis, so the divergent tail stays visible beneath the near-identical spike.") +
  base_theme +
  # The facet strips already name the two groups; a colour key would repeat them.
  guides(fill = "none")

# ============================================================================
# Panel B -- where the 493 dark OTUs land
# ============================================================================
asum <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "E1_SH_assignment_summary.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(asum) == 1L)
bdf <- data.frame(
  cat = factor(unname(sh_class_map[c("placeable_existing_SH", "novel_new_SH",
                                     "no_SH_match", "excluded_nonITS")]),
               levels = SH_LEVELS),
  n   = c(asum$placeable_existing_SH, asum$novel_new_SH,
          asum$no_SH_match, asum$excluded_nonITS))
# Drift guard: the committed summary must still agree with the per-OTU table.
tab_dark <- table(factor(unname(sh_class_map[sh$SH_class[sh$is_dark]]), levels = SH_LEVELS))
stopifnot(sum(bdf$n) == asum$n_dark, asum$n_dark == sum(sh$is_dark),
          identical(as.integer(tab_dark[SH_LEVELS]), as.integer(bdf$n)))
bdf$pct <- 100 * bdf$n / asum$n_dark
bdf$cat <- factor(bdf$cat, levels = rev(SH_LEVELS))   # first category at the top

pB <- ggplot(bdf, aes(n, cat, fill = cat)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.68, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d  (%.0f%%)", n, pct)), hjust = -0.12,
            size = 3.1, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sh_cols, name = "UNITE SH placement", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.40))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(" to existing SH", "\nto existing SH", x)) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Dark OTUs (n = %d)", asum$n_dark), y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Every OTU with no confident\ngenus assignment.") +
  base_theme +
  guides(fill = "none")

# ============================================================================
# Panel C -- the winter-abundant dark OTUs
# ============================================================================
# The committed top-30-by-winter-read-share table, so the panel's membership is a
# published definition rather than a threshold invented for the figure.
wd <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "E1_winter_dominant_dark_taxa_SH.csv"),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(wd) == 30L, all(wd$winter_n == 26L), all(wd$OTU_ID %in% sh$OTU_ID))
wd$cat <- factor(unname(sh_class_map[wd$SH_class]), levels = SH_LEVELS)
wd$share_pct <- 100 * wd$winter_mean_share
# Drift guard: this table must be the top 30 of the per-OTU table it came from.
top30 <- sh$OTU_ID[sh$is_dark][order(-sh$winter_mean_share[sh$is_dark])][1:30]
stopifnot(setequal(wd$OTU_ID, top30))

lab <- wd[wd$OTU_ID == "OTU1369", ]
stopifnot(nrow(lab) == 1L, lab$winter_occ == 20L)     # agrees with Fig. 3D
lab$txt <- sprintf("OTU1369\ncandidate novel SH, %.0f%% id\n%.1f%% of winter reads, %d/%d samples",
                   lab$similarity_percentage, lab$share_pct, lab$winter_occ, lab$winter_n)

pC <- ggplot(wd, aes(winter_occ, share_pct, fill = cat)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3.2, colour = "grey25", stroke = 0.4, alpha = 0.9) +
  # Hung below-left of the marker rather than centred on it, so the point stays
  # visibly a data point instead of reading as punctuation inside the text.
  geom_text(data = lab, aes(label = txt), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            x = lab$winter_occ - 0.8, y = lab$share_pct - 0.7, hjust = 1, vjust = 1,
            size = 2.9, lineheight = 1.05, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sh_cols, name = "UNITE SH placement", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 26), breaks = seq(0, 25, 5),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.10))) +
  labs(x = sprintf("Prevalence (winter samples with a detection, of %d)", wd$winter_n[1]),
       y = "Mean winter read share (%)",
       subtitle = "The 30 dark OTUs with the highest\nmean winter read share (Table S-E1b).") +
  base_theme +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3.4)))

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
# Explicit design grid rather than nested `/` and `|`: patchwork FLATTENS a chain
# of `/`, so (pA) / (pB | pC) would silently become a three-row layout.
design <- "
AAAAAAAA
BBBCCCCC
"
fig4 <- pA + pB + pC +
  plot_layout(design = design, heights = c(1, 1.02), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal")

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  one(function() grDevices::png(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                                units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  pdf_dev <- if (capabilities("cairo")) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  one(function() pdf_dev(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig4_dark_taxa_SH"), fig4, 10, 8.8)

# ---- console summary -------------------------------------------------------
cat("Best-hit similarity, by group:\n")
print(data.frame(group = G_LEVELS,
                 n_with_hit = as.integer(table(sim$group)[G_LEVELS]),
                 no_best_hit = as.integer(n_nosim),
                 median_id = round(as.numeric(tapply(sim$similarity_percentage, sim$group, median)[G_LEVELS]), 2),
                 pct_ge99 = round(100 * as.numeric(tapply(sim$similarity_percentage, sim$group,
                                                          function(x) mean(x >= 99))[G_LEVELS]), 1),
                 pct_lt95 = round(100 * as.numeric(tapply(sim$similarity_percentage, sim$group,
                                                          function(x) mean(x < 95))[G_LEVELS]), 1)),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nDark OTUs (n = %d) by SH placement:\n", asum$n_dark))
print(data.frame(placement = as.character(bdf$cat), n = bdf$n, pct = round(bdf$pct, 1)),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nTop 10 winter-abundant dark OTUs:\n")
o <- order(-wd$share_pct)[1:10]
print(data.frame(OTU = wd$OTU_ID[o], class = sub("^c__", "", wd$Class[o]),
                 winter_pct = round(wd$share_pct[o], 2),
                 prevalence = sprintf("%d/%d", wd$winter_occ[o], wd$winter_n[o]),
                 id = wd$similarity_percentage[o],
                 placement = as.character(wd$cat[o])), row.names = FALSE)
```

### 10.5 Figure 5 — A reproducible seasonal axis inside large among-individual variation (HMSC synthesis)

*Provenance: Fig. 5A is the occurrence-scale per-OTU niche of Section 9.4 (Table S-HMSCe(iii)), with the guild means that reproduce the trait → environment link of Section 9.3 (Table S-HMSCd); Fig. 5B is the variance partition of Section 9.2 (Table S-HMSCc). Both panels read the committed `tables/hmsc_*.csv` written by `10_hmsc.R`, so the figure cannot drift from Section 9.*

![](figures/main/Fig5_hmsc_synthesis.png)

**Figure 5**: A joint species distribution model resolves a consistent seasonal axis at OTU level while showing how small it is against variation among individual droppings. **(A)** Per-OTU Season coefficient from the presence/absence (probit) HMSC model — positive = more likely to occur in summer — for the 25 most summer- and 25 most winter-shifted of the 226 modelled OTUs, coloured by functional guild, with 95% credible intervals; filled points are the 35 of these 50 whose interval excludes zero. The lower block gives each guild's mean of the per-OTU estimates (diamond) with the interquartile range, over all OTUs in that guild rather than only the 50 plotted; these means reproduce the trait-level Gamma coefficients of Table S-HMSCd to within 0.04. **(B)** Mean share of per-OTU variance in CLR abundance attributed to Season, Year, the biological-sample random level and the PCR-replicate random level, for all 226 OTUs and within each guild (Table S-HMSCc). Panel A comes from the occurrence formulation and panel B from the abundance formulation, following the division of labour set out in Section 9.1: the probit model is the one whose per-OTU niches converge cleanly (Beta median PSRF 1.01, 99.6% of parameters below 1.1), while the variance partition is well behaved in the CLR model. The five guild classes are the model's trait and differ slightly from the display split used in Figure 1 — 46 OTUs carrying a genus but no FUNGuild call sit in "Other assigned" here and in "Unassigned / dark" there (`tables/guild_scheme_crosswalk.csv`, Section 8.1).

Panel A makes the seasonal signal concrete at the level of individual lineages, and it is sharper in occurrence than in abundance: 55 of 226 OTUs have a Season coefficient whose 95% credible interval excludes zero, against 4 in the abundance model. The direction is overwhelmingly one-way — 157 of 226 OTUs shift towards summer, with a community median of +0.70 — so summer dung does not merely contain different fungi, it contains more kinds of fungi that are reliably present. The winter extreme is the familiar one: dark, taxonomically unresolved lineages (14 of the 25 most winter-shifted) together with pathotrophs, led by OTU1369, the most winter-shifted OTU in the community and the same unclassified Dothideomycete that dominates winter read share in Figure 4. The summer extreme, however, is *not* led by the coprophilous fungi. It is dominated by cold-adapted basidiomycete yeasts — *Vishniacozyma*, *Mrakia*, *Piskurozyma*, *Phenoliferia* — and by dark taxa, with *Sporormiella* (OTU636) the only dung saprotroph among the top 25. This is a real distinction rather than a contradiction of Figure 1: the coprophiles are what summer dung is *made of* in read share, but they are not what most reliably *appears* in summer, and the guild means in the lower block of panel A show the same ordering as the trait model (yeast-rich "other" +0.79, plant-associated +0.59, dung saprotroph +0.44, dark +0.37, pathotroph +0.07 — the only guild with no summer tendency). Panel B then supplies the scale that keeps all of this in proportion. Season and Year together account for about 20% of per-OTU variance (Season 11.2%, Year 8.4%), and the Season share is remarkably even across guilds (9.0% for plant-associated taxa to 14.3% for pathotrophs), while roughly half of the variance sits among biological samples — one dropping to the next — and a further third among PCR replicates of the same dropping. The community-mean Season share independently recovers the PERMANOVA R² of 0.11 from Section 4 with a completely different model. Taken together the two panels state the study's central quantitative claim in one place: seasonal turnover is real, directional, and reproducible across methods, yet it is modest beside the idiosyncrasy of individual birds — which is why the model explains the samples it has seen (R² ≈ 0.46) but cannot predict one it has not (Section 9.7).

```{r fig5-build}
#| eval: false
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Full build code for Figure 5 — the source of truth for figures/main/Fig5_hmsc_synthesis.{png,jpg,pdf}"

# Figure 5 -- HMSC synthesis: per-OTU seasonal niche + variance partition.
# Every number is READ from the committed tables/ CSVs written by 10_hmsc.R; no
# model is loaded or refitted here (the fits are ~200 MB each and the figure
# needs only their posterior summaries).
#   A  tables/hmsc_probit_beta_season.csv  (per-OTU Season Beta, probit/occurrence)
#      tables/hmsc_probit_gamma_CrI.csv    (trait-level Gamma -- used as a GUARD)
#      tables/hmsc_convergence_psrf.csv    (printed into the panel subtitle)
#   B  tables/hmsc_variance_partition.csv  (per-OTU variance components, CLR)
# Panel A is the occurrence model and panel B the abundance model, per the
# division of labour in Section 9.1: only the probit Beta converges cleanly,
# only the CLR model yields the variance partition.
# Rebuild:  conda run -n r_env Rscript build_main_figure.R fig5-build

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(patchwork); library(ggtext)
})

tab_dir <- if (dir.exists("tables")) "tables" else
           "/home/daniel/Ptarmigan/Scripts_server/Supplementary/tables"
out_dir <- "figures/main"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
grDevices::pdf(NULL)                                 # headless: no X11 fallback

# ---- shared style ----------------------------------------------------------
# Guild colours are Figure 1's, so a guild is the same colour in every main
# figure. The model's five-level trait is NOT identical to Figure 1's display
# split (46 OTUs move between "Other assigned" and "Unassigned / dark"); the
# caption says so and tables/guild_scheme_crosswalk.csv reconciles them.
GUILD_LEVELS <- c("Dung saprotroph", "Plant-associated", "Pathotroph",
                  "Other assigned", "Unassigned / dark")
guild_cols <- c("Dung saprotroph" = "#E69F00", "Plant-associated" = "#009E73",
                "Pathotroph" = "#CC79A7", "Other assigned" = "#56B4E9",
                "Unassigned / dark" = "#999999")
guild_map <- c(dung_saprotroph = "Dung saprotroph", plant_associated = "Plant-associated",
               pathotroph = "Pathotroph", other = "Other assigned",
               dark_unassigned = "Unassigned / dark")
# Variance components deliberately share NO colour with the guild scale, and
# split fixed (coloured) from random (grey): the visual point of panel B is how
# little of the bar is coloured.
VP_LEVELS <- c("Season", "Year", "Random: sample", "Random: pcr")   # CSV column names
# Displayed names: the CSV's terse "Random: pcr" is fine in a supplementary
# table but a main-text key has to say what the level actually is.
vp_display <- c("Season" = "Season", "Year" = "Year",
                "Random: sample" = "Biological sample (dropping)",
                "Random: pcr"    = "PCR replicate")
vp_cols <- c("Season" = "#0072B2", "Year" = "#F0E442",
             "Biological sample (dropping)" = "#666666", "PCR replicate" = "#CCCCCC")

base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5, angle = 0),
        plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.spacing    = unit(0.5, "lines"),
        legend.key.size  = unit(0.42, "cm"),
        legend.title     = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.text      = element_text(size = 9))

# All in-plot text is ASCII: save_fig() falls back to grDevices::pdf when cairo
# is unavailable, and that device silently substitutes a dot for a Unicode glyph.
# (The markdown asterisks below are ggtext italics markup, and are ASCII.)

# ============================================================================
# Panel A -- per-OTU seasonal niche (probit), plus guild means
# ============================================================================
b <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_probit_beta_season.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(b) == 226L, !anyNA(b$beta_season_mean), !anyNA(b$beta_season_CrI2.5),
          setequal(b$guild, names(guild_map)))
b$Guild <- factor(unname(guild_map[b$guild]), levels = GUILD_LEVELS)
b <- b[order(-b$beta_season_mean), ]

# The 25 most summer- and 25 most winter-shifted OTUs.
sel <- rbind(head(b, 25), tail(b, 25))
stopifnot(nrow(sel) == 50L, !any(duplicated(sel$OTU_ID)))

# Row labels: genus in italics via ggtext, but only where "Genus" really is a
# genus -- Incertae sedis placeholders are family-level and are not italicised.
lab_of <- function(otu, gen) {
  ifelse(is.na(gen), otu,
  ifelse(grepl("Incertae", gen, fixed = TRUE),
         paste0(otu, " (", sub("_gen_Incertae_sedis", "", gen), ")"),
         paste0(otu, " (*", gen, "*)")))
}
sel$lab <- lab_of(sel$OTU_ID, sel$Genus)
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(sel$lab)))
# Support is one-sided P(beta > 0); a two-sided 95% CrI excluding zero is the
# stricter statement, so THAT is what the filled points mark.
sel$resolved <- factor(ifelse(sel$beta_season_CrI2.5 > 0 | sel$beta_season_CrI97.5 < 0,
                              "95% CrI excludes 0", "CrI overlaps 0"),
                       levels = c("95% CrI excludes 0", "CrI overlaps 0"))

# Guild means over ALL OTUs of that guild (not just the 50 plotted), with the
# IQR of the same per-OTU estimates as a spread -- a summary of the points
# above, NOT a credible interval, which is why it is drawn as a plain segment.
gm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(GUILD_LEVELS, function(g) {
  v <- b$beta_season_mean[b$Guild == g]
  data.frame(Guild = factor(g, levels = GUILD_LEVELS), n = length(v),
             mean = mean(v), q25 = quantile(v, 0.25), q75 = quantile(v, 0.75),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
gm$lab <- sprintf("%s (n = %d)", as.character(gm$Guild), gm$n)

# Drift guard: these guild means must reproduce the trait-level Gamma of
# Table S-HMSCd (reference guild = dung saprotroph, other rows are deviations
# from it). They are not algebraically identical -- Gamma is a hierarchical
# mean, not the arithmetic mean of Beta -- so the tolerance is loose enough to
# allow shrinkage but tight enough to catch a mismatched table.
gam <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_probit_gamma_CrI.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
gam <- gam[gam$covariate == "Seasonsummer", ]
gref <- gam$mean[gam$trait == "(Intercept)"]
gimp <- setNames(c(gref, gref + gam$mean[match(paste0("guild", names(guild_map)[-1]), gam$trait)]),
                 unname(guild_map))
stopifnot(!anyNA(gimp[as.character(gm$Guild)]),
          max(abs(gm$mean - gimp[as.character(gm$Guild)])) < 0.10)

# One plot, two blocks: facet_grid with free space gives the guild block a
# height proportional to its 5 rows and keeps ONE shared x axis and one tag.
BLOCKS <- c("Per-OTU niche", "Guild mean")   # short: the lower block is only 5 rows tall
otu_df <- data.frame(lab = sel$lab, Guild = sel$Guild, resolved = sel$resolved,
                     est = sel$beta_season_mean,
                     lo = sel$beta_season_CrI2.5, hi = sel$beta_season_CrI97.5,
                     block = factor(BLOCKS[1], levels = BLOCKS))
gm_df  <- data.frame(lab = gm$lab, Guild = gm$Guild, est = gm$mean,
                     lo = gm$q25, hi = gm$q75,
                     block = factor(BLOCKS[2], levels = BLOCKS))
lvl <- c(gm_df$lab[order(gm_df$est)], otu_df$lab[order(otu_df$est)])
otu_df$lab <- factor(otu_df$lab, levels = lvl)
gm_df$lab  <- factor(gm_df$lab,  levels = lvl)

conv <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_convergence_psrf.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cpa  <- conv[conv$model == "pa", ]
stopifnot(nrow(cpa) == 1L)
n_res <- sum(sel$resolved == "95% CrI excludes 0")

pA <- ggplot(otu_df, aes(est, lab, colour = Guild)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey70") +
  # geom_segment rather than geom_errorbarh: the latter is deprecated in
  # ggplot2 4.0 and its replacement's argument names differ between versions.
  geom_segment(aes(x = lo, xend = hi, y = lab, yend = lab), linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = resolved), size = 1.9, stroke = 0.7) +
  # guild block: IQR segment behind, mean diamond on top, value printed
  geom_segment(data = gm_df, aes(x = lo, xend = hi, y = lab, yend = lab),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = gm_df, aes(est, lab, fill = Guild), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 23, size = 3, colour = "grey20", stroke = 0.4) +
  # Value printed to the RIGHT of the IQR, not above the diamond: the five guild
  # means sit within 0.7 of each other, so a label above one row lands on the next.
  geom_text(data = gm_df, aes(hi, lab, label = sprintf("%+.2f", est)), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.12, size = 2.7, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(block), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = guild_cols, name = "Guild", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = guild_cols, guide = "none", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("95% CrI excludes 0" = 16, "CrI overlaps 0" = 1),
                     name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "HMSC Beta: Season (probit, positive = more likely in summer)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0("25 most summer- and 25 most winter-shifted of 226 OTUs; %d of 50 resolved.\n",
                                 "Occurrence model, Beta PSRF median %.2f (%.1f%% of parameters < 1.1)."),
                          n_res, cpa$beta_psrf_med, cpa$beta_pct_below_1.1)) +
  base_theme +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_markdown(size = 6.6),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold", size = 8)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(shape = 16, size = 2.6)),
         shape  = guide_legend(order = 2))

# ============================================================================
# Panel B -- variance partition (CLR), community-wide and by guild
# ============================================================================
vp <- read.csv(file.path(tab_dir, "hmsc_variance_partition.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
# Components are stored rounded to 4 dp, so a row sums to 1 only to within the
# rounding error of four values -- hence 1e-3 rather than machine tolerance.
stopifnot(nrow(vp) == 226L, setequal(vp$OTU_ID, b$OTU_ID),
          all(VP_LEVELS %in% names(vp)),
          max(abs(rowSums(vp[, VP_LEVELS]) - 1)) < 1e-3)
vp$Guild <- factor(unname(guild_map[vp$guild]), levels = GUILD_LEVELS)

grp_mean <- function(d, label) data.frame(
  grp = label, n = nrow(d),
  t(colMeans(d[, VP_LEVELS])), check.names = FALSE)
vpm <- rbind(grp_mean(vp, "All OTUs"),
             do.call(rbind, lapply(GUILD_LEVELS,
                                   function(g) grp_mean(vp[vp$Guild == g, ], g))))
vpm$lab <- sprintf("%s (n = %d)", vpm$grp, vpm$n)
# Drift guard: the community-mean Season share is quoted as ~11% in Section 9.2
# and Table S-HMSCc, and matched against the PERMANOVA R2 of 0.11 in Section 4.
stopifnot(abs(100 * vpm$Season[vpm$grp == "All OTUs"] - 11.2) < 0.15)

vpL <- data.frame(
  lab  = factor(rep(vpm$lab, times = length(VP_LEVELS)), levels = rev(vpm$lab)),
  comp = factor(rep(unname(vp_display[VP_LEVELS]), each = nrow(vpm)),
                levels = unname(vp_display[VP_LEVELS])),
  pct  = 100 * unlist(vpm[, VP_LEVELS], use.names = FALSE))
# Season is the one segment whose exact value the reader needs; print it inside.
seaslab <- vpL[vpL$comp == "Season", ]
seaslab$mid <- seaslab$pct / 2
fixedlab <- data.frame(lab = factor(vpm$lab, levels = rev(vpm$lab)),
                       txt = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * (vpm$Season + vpm$Year)))

pB <- ggplot(vpL, aes(pct, lab, fill = comp)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25,
           position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(data = seaslab, aes(mid, lab, label = sprintf("%.1f", pct)), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 2.9, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = fixedlab, aes(103, lab, label = txt), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = vp_cols, name = "Variance component") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.16)),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(" \\(n = ", "\n(n = ", x)) +
  labs(x = "Mean share of per-OTU variance", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Abundance (CLR) model; all 226 OTUs, then by guild.\nRight-hand figures give Season + Year combined.") +
  base_theme +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = 0.95)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

# ---- assemble and write ----------------------------------------------------
fig5 <- (pA | pB) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  # Three collected keys (guild, support, variance component) do not fit on one
  # row at this width -- side by side they overflow the device and are clipped.
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.box.just = "left", legend.margin = margin(t = 0, b = 0))

# Every main figure is written three ways: PNG and JPG (600 dpi raster, for
# submission systems that demand one or the other) and PDF (vector, for print).
save_fig <- function(stem, obj, width, height, res = 600) {
  one <- function(open_dev) { open_dev(); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()); print(obj) }
  one(function() grDevices::png(paste0(stem, ".png"), width = width, height = height,
                                units = "in", res = res))
  one(function() grDevices::jpeg(paste0(stem, ".jpg"), width = width, height = height,
                                 units = "in", res = res, quality = 95))
  pdf_dev <- if (capabilities("cairo")) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf
  one(function() pdf_dev(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), width = width, height = height))
}
save_fig(file.path(out_dir, "Fig5_hmsc_synthesis"), fig5, 11.5, 9.5)

# ---- console summary -------------------------------------------------------
cat(sprintf("Per-OTU Season Beta (probit): %d of %d OTUs with a 95%% CrI excluding 0; %d of the 50 plotted.\n",
            sum(b$beta_season_CrI2.5 > 0 | b$beta_season_CrI97.5 < 0), nrow(b), n_res))
cat(sprintf("Community shift: median %+.2f, %d of %d OTUs positive.\n",
            median(b$beta_season_mean), sum(b$beta_season_mean > 0), nrow(b)))
cat("\nGuild means vs the trait-level Gamma (Table S-HMSCd):\n")
print(data.frame(guild = as.character(gm$Guild), n = gm$n,
                 mean_beta = round(gm$mean, 3),
                 gamma_implied = round(unname(gimp[as.character(gm$Guild)]), 3),
                 IQR = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", gm$q25, gm$q75)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nExtremes of panel A:\n")
print(data.frame(end = c(rep("summer", 3), rep("winter", 3)),
                 OTU = c(head(sel$OTU_ID, 3), rev(tail(sel$OTU_ID, 3))),
                 guild = as.character(c(head(sel$Guild, 3), rev(tail(sel$Guild, 3)))),
                 beta = round(c(head(sel$beta_season_mean, 3), rev(tail(sel$beta_season_mean, 3))), 2)),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nGuild composition of the 25 summer- / 25 winter-shifted rows:\n")
print(table(guild = sel$Guild, end = rep(c("summer25", "winter25"), each = 25)))
cat("\nVariance partition (mean % per OTU):\n")
print(data.frame(group = vpm$lab, round(100 * vpm[, VP_LEVELS], 1), check.names = FALSE),
      row.names = FALSE)
```
